PositiveEntailmentTest.purpose: This test highlights the different behavior of forward-chaining vs. backward-chaining engines
PositiveEntailmentTest.description: The entailment holds, but some engines may have difficulty finding it and/or may behave badly with it. This particular test case may be hard to handle for backward-chaining engines, depending on their implementation of the func:numeric-add builtin. In a forward-chaining strategy, the entailment should be found, but since the minimal model itself is infinite, a naive engine, which tries to materialize the whole minimal model may not terminate.

Group ( Forall ?x ( ex:a(External(func:numeric-add(?x 1))) :- ex:a(?x) ) ex:a(1) ) )

PositiveEntailmentTest.purpose: This test highlights the different behavior of forward-chaining vs. backward-chaining engines
PositiveEntailmentTest.description: The entailment holds, but some engines may have difficulty finding it and/or may behave badly with it. This particular test case may be hard to handle for backward-chaining engines, depending on their implementation of the func:numeric-subtract builtin. In a forward-chaining strategy, the entailment should be found. Note that a backward-chaining engine, which is able to handle the external built-in in the head would avoid non-termination problems on arbitrary other entailment tests with this ruleset by the termination condition in the body.

PositiveEntailmentTest.purpose: This test shows a sample scenario related to exchanging electronic business contracts across rule platforms.

PositiveEntailmentTest.description: The syntax for constants in RIF and RDF is slightly different; RDF has a number of different kinds of constants (e.g., IRI, in a literal, typed literal), whereas RIF has a single kind of constant (i.e., a pair <literal, symbol space>). NegativeEntailmentTest.purpose: Test interaction between rdfs:subClassOf, rdf:type, ## and # in RIF
NegativeEntailmentTest.description: In RIF-RDF combinations, we have that rdf:type statements are equivalent to RIF # statements and RIF ## statements imply rdfs:subClassOf statements. By the semantics of combinations, we have that ex:a rdf:type ex:C implies ex:a # ex:C, but ex:C rdfs:subClassOf ex:D does not imply ex:C ## ex:D. Therefore, ex:a # ex:D cannot be derived. Notice that the import profile is 'Simple'.

PositiveEntailmentTest.purpose: Test interaction between rdfs:subClassOf, rdf:type, ## and # in RIF
PositiveEntailmentTest.description: In RIF-RDF combinations, we have that rdf:type statements are equivalent to RIF # statements and RIF ## statements imply rdfs:subClassOf statements. By the RDFS semantics we have that ex:a rdf:type ex:D must hold and by the semantics of combinations, we have that ex:a rdf:type ex:D implies ex:a # ex:D. Therefore, ex:a # ex:D is derived.
